Hi all — quick legal/technical read. I pulled the Acme DPA and relevant SOW: there is a contractual obligation to notify "affected customers" without undue delay when there is a breach of security resulting in unauthorized access to PII or secrets; the DPA does not enumerate telemetry specifically, so we need to determine whether telemetry from the bucket qualifies as "personal data" under the contract and relevant regulators.

Technical preservation checklist (recommended, immediate):
- Create immutable snapshot (S3 object version + MD5 manifest).
- Export server access logs for the implicated host (range: 2026-11-20 to present).
- Preserve application-layer logs that map tokens -> account ids; if mapping exists, flag entries as likely "affected".
- Generate a signed hash manifest for chain of custody.

Jurisdiction note: Acme has EU-based customers in scope; if personal data belonging to EU residents is involved, we must avoid unnecessary export of raw logs to non-EU processors without Legal signoff. Suggest redaction at source and request guidance from Acme Legal on what minimal export is acceptable.

Proposed timeline:
- 8 hours: snapshot + preserve (evidence manifest attached).
- 48 hours: preliminary scope call with Acme + high-level findings (yes/no on PII/secrets).
- 7 days: forensic report draft.

I will coordinate with ForensicsCo if Acme asks for that vendor. Attaching the list of CLI commands and a short evidence manifest template.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security
